sections.html:
The Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder files deeds, deeds of trust and other land documents for the county. Go to the Recording Division in the Administration and Courts building, 100 Jefferson County Parkway, Suite 2560, Golden, CO 80419. The phone is 303-271-8168. Visits can be booked online on the county recording page.

The counter is open Monday to Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., and opens at 8 a.m. on the third Thursday of each month. Call before you plan a Friday visit. Otherwise, drop the deed off early in the week, mail it, or send it through an approved e-recording vendor.

Once recorded, a document joins the public record and the county archives. That step is what puts a buyer's name on the title for anyone who searches later. Jefferson County runs from city blocks in Lakewood to canyon lots near Conifer, with Golden as the county seat, but every deed goes through this one office.

Most letter or legal size documents carry a flat $43 recording fee, however many pages they run. A state documentary fee applies on top for transfer deeds with consideration above $500.

Document or serviceFee
Standard document up to 8.5 x 14 inches$43 flat per document
Plats and documents larger than 8.5 x 14 inches$40 per document
Documentary fee on a deed$0.10 per $1,000 of consideration when it exceeds $500
Digital copiesFree
Certification of a copy$1 per document
Documents tied to a death recordFree

State law, C.R.S. 39-13-102, sets the documentary fee at one cent per $100 of consideration. The person who submits the deed pays it, and the clerk collects it with the recording fee. Phone the office for a total before you mail a check.

Bring a standard size deed to the counter, mail it, or use an approved e-recording vendor. Large format documents cannot be taken in person and must go through a vendor.

  • In person: standard size documents only, at the Golden office during counter hours.
  • By mail: send the document, the right payment, a return mailing address and a phone number.
  • E-recording: required for large format items. Plats can be recorded electronically only through the county's contracted vendor.

Mail is the slowest route, with returned documents taking 2 to 4 weeks. The county refunds only overpayments of $10 or more, so a short check can hold up the whole filing. Escrow and title companies usually handle this step in a sale. When a deed moves outside a formal closing, the person sending it carries the risk.

Colorado law requires the grantee's address on the recorded document. Clerks cannot tell you which legal form to use, so have the deed drafted and checked before it reaches the counter.

Consideration matters too. For the documentary fee, property is treated as residential unless the instrument clearly says otherwise. A deed that states no consideration, or $500 or less, can still be measured against the sales price on a related declaration, so understating the price does not make the fee go away.

  • Names of the grantor and grantee as they appear on the prior deed.
  • A legal description, not just a street address.
  • The grantee's mailing address.
  • A statement of consideration, so the fee is figured on the right number.

sections.h2: The Public Trustee and loan payoffs
sections.html:
The Jefferson County Public Trustee handles foreclosures of deeds of trust and releases of deeds of trust recorded through its office. It is at Suite 2510 of the same building, phone 303-271-8580. Public Trustee fees rose under HB 25-1269 on July 1, 2025.

Releases for private trustee mortgage transactions go to the Clerk and Recorder instead, at 303-271-8121. If an old lien was never released, a buyer's lender or title company may refuse to move forward, so check the record early.

Judicial foreclosures belong to the Sheriff, not the Public Trustee. Foreclosure records stay public even after a default is cured or a foreclosure is withdrawn.

The county offers a free Recording Notification Service that sends an alert when a document is recorded in your name. Signing up helps you catch a forged deed or a lien you never authorized.

The office will never ask for payment by wire transfer. If an unexpected email or call demands money for a recording, treat it as a scam and phone the office at a number from the county site.

Homes in the unincorporated wildland urban interface fall under the Jefferson County Wildfire Resiliency Code, approved March 10, 2026 and effective July 1, 2026. It is not retroactive. It covers new construction and exterior alterations such as additions, deck replacements, re-siding and re-roofing.

A roof replacement covering 25% or more of the roof must be a Class A assembly, and siding replacement of 25% or more must use allowed materials. Smaller repairs, interior work and painting are exempt. The defensible space page describes three zones out to 100 feet from a structure.

A seller in Conifer, Pine or the canyons who starts a roof or deck project before listing can trigger permit steps. Selling as is, without starting that work, avoids them. County staff say no grants are offered, though the SLASH program takes defensible space debris at reduced cost.

A rejected or delayed filing costs weeks. Run through this short list before the deed leaves your hands.

  1. Match the grantor's name to the prior deed.
  2. Confirm the legal description and the grantee's mailing address are on the page.
  3. Decide how it will travel: counter, mail or vendor.
  4. Add the recording fee and any documentary fee, then ask the office for the total.
  5. Include a return address and phone number if you mail it.

sections.h2: Other offices a seller deals with
sections.html:
Besides the recorder, most sellers touch three more offices: the Assessor for value, the Treasurer for taxes and the Public Trustee for liens. Each has its own timing.

  • Assessor: real property appeals run May 1 through June 8 each year.
  • Treasurer: taxes are paid in arrears, so 2025 taxes were payable in 2026, and the notice goes out in late January.
  • Public Trustee: any recorded deed of trust needs a release before the title is clean.
  • Recorder: the new deed has to go in with the right fee and a grantee address.

A cash sale to a direct buyer skips showings and lender conditions, which suits a house with deferred repairs, an inherited title or a stack of back taxes. The recording steps above still apply to every sale in the county.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Jefferson County, Colorado?
faqs.a: A flat $43 per standard size document, plus a state documentary fee of $0.10 per $1,000 of consideration on deeds above $500. Large plats and oversize documents are $40 each. Phone the office to confirm the total before you mail payment.

faqs.q: Does Jefferson County, CO charge a transfer tax?
faqs.a: Colorado imposes a documentary fee of one cent per $100 of consideration, paid by whoever submits the deed.

faqs.q: How long does a mailed deed take to come back recorded?
faqs.a: Returned documents take 2 to 4 weeks by mail. Overpayments of $10 or more are refunded, but a payment that is too low can delay the filing.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in person on a Friday?
faqs.a: Counter hours are Monday to Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Call 303-271-8168 before a Friday visit, or use mail or e-recording.

faqs.q: Who releases an old deed of trust in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Releases handled through the Public Trustee go through that office at 303-271-8580. Releases for private trustee mortgage transactions go to the Clerk and Recorder at 303-271-8121.
